name: task
description: The "task" field outlines the specific requirements and objectives for generating the content. This includes detailed instructions on what needs to be accomplished through the writing, such as the main topic to be covered, any particular arguments or perspectives to be presented, and the desired outcome or impact of the piece. This field serves as a directive for the content creation process, ensuring that the writing not only adheres to the given guidelines but also effectively achieves its intended purpose, whether it's to inform, persuade, entertain, or educate the audience.

name: language
description: Required, the language used by the user in the request, according to the ISO 639-1 standard. For Chinese, use zh-CN for Simplified Chinese and zh-TW for Traditional Chinese.

name: summary
description: The "summary" field encapsulates a concise overview of the writing content, presenting the core themes, key points, and primary objectives of the piece. This brief but comprehensive synopsis serves as a roadmap, guiding the overall direction and focus of the writing, ensuring that it remains aligned with the intended message and purpose throughout the development process. This summary not only aids in maintaining coherence and relevance but also provides a clear preview of what the reader can expect from the full content.

name: reference
description: The "reference" field is a curated collection of information sourced from the Internet via WebPilot, or proveded by the user, specifically tailored to enrich and support the writing task at hand. It involves a selective process where relevant data, facts, and insights related to the topic are gathered, ensuring that the content is not only well-informed and accurate but also closely aligned with the specific requirements and objectives of the writing project. This field acts as a foundation, providing a rich base of verified and pertinent information from which the article or content is crafted. This field would be long.

name: style
description: The "style" field in content creation is a detailed framework encompassing three pivotal components - the writing tone or style, the target audience, and the publication medium. This field is structured as "[specific writing style], aimed at [target audience], using [language style], inspired by [notable content creator]." The writing style element ranges from formal and analytical to casual and engaging, setting the overall tone. The target audience aspect identifies the specific reader group, such as students, professionals, or the general public, tailoring the content's complexity and relevance. The language style, whether academic, colloquial, or technical, shapes the linguistic approach. The final component, inspired by a notable content creator, serves as a reference for the desired tone and approach, like "analytical and concise, aimed at business professionals, using professional language, inspired by a renowned business journalist." This clear and structured definition ensures the content is effectively aligned with the audience's needs and the publication's format.

name: style
description: The "style" field in content creation is a comprehensive framework that includes four essential components - the writing tone or style, the target audience, the language style, and inspiration from a notable content creator. This field is structured as "[specific writing style], aimed at [target audience], using [language style], and inspired by [notable content creator]." The writing style element, which should convey warmth and human empathy, ranges from formal and analytical to casual and engaging, setting the overall tone. The target audience aspect identifies the specific reader group, such as students, professionals, or the general public, ensuring the content's complexity and relevance are appropriately tailored. The language style, whether academic, colloquial, or technical, shapes the linguistic approach, infusing it with a sense of human touch and concern. The final component, inspired by a notable content creator, serves as a reference for the desired tone and approach, like "analytical and concise, yet warm and empathetic, aimed at business professionals, using professional language, inspired by a renowned business journalist." This clear, structured definition, enriched with emotional depth and humanistic care, ensures the content is effectively aligned with the audience's needs and the publication's format.

description: A query to find relevant research papers. To search effectively, ask research questions related to scientific topics, such as 'the future of manipulation of genes and DNA' or 'the benefits of the study of genes and heredity'. Ask broad yes/no questions, inquire about the relationship between concepts, or ask about the effects or impact of a concept. Use technical language where possible to maximize the relevance to academic text. For example, if the user asks 'Why do some foods taste sweet and others taste sour?', search 'What causes different taste sensations in foods?'. Remove unnecessary commands like 'latest research' and 'find papers' and focus only on words likely to match with the text of research papers.

name: yearMin
description: The earliest publication year to consider in the search, filtering out papers published before this year. You must only use this filter when the user asks for information after a certain date. An example of when to use this filter would be if a user asks 'Show me articles about renewable energy published after 2020.' or 'Find research papers about artificial intelligence published between 2015 and 2020.'. If you use this filter without the user specifically including a date or 'recent research', you will be penalized.

name: yearMax
description: The latest publication year to consider in the search, filtering out papers published after this year. You must only use this filter when the user asks for information before a certain date. An example of when to use this filter would be if a user asks 'Show me scientific studies on climate change published before 2023' or 'Find research papers about artificial intelligence published between 2015 and 2020.'. Only use this filter when a specific year restriction is requested by the user

Since our Free plan contains 100 free SERP proxies, and every request consumes 1 proxy, you will get exactly 100 free requests, no matter the amount of results you will get per each.

name: date_range
description:
An object that should contain either "date_preset" or both "start_date" and "end_date".
- For example: {"date_preset": "last_7_days"} or {"start_date": "2020-01-01", "end_date": "2020-01-31"} or {"date_preset": "last_week"}.
- "date_preset": A predefined date range; must be one of these values: today,yesterday,this_week_sun_today,this_week_mon_today,last_week,last_3_weeks,last_week_sun_sat,last_week_mon_sun,this_month,last_month,last_3_months,last_6_months,this_quarter,last_7_days,last_14_days,last_30_days,last_60_days,last_90_days,this_year,last_year.
- "start_date": The start date of the date range to query, format: YYYY-MM-DD. Optional if "date_preset" is provided.
- "end_date": The end date of the date range to query, format: YYYY-MM-DD. Optional if "date_preset" is provided.
- Here are some examples of how users might ask for date ranges:
    - "past 7 days" should be {"date_preset": "last_7_days"}.
    - "last week" should be {"date_preset": "last_week"}.
    - "last 3 weeks" should be {"date_preset": "last_3_weeks"}.
    - "this month" should be {"date_preset": "this_month"}.
    - "last 6 month" should be {"date_preset": "last_6_months"}.
    - "June 2023" should be {"start_date": "2023-06-01", "end_date": "2023-06-30"}.
    - "from Jan 2023 to June 2023" should be {"start_date": "2023-01-01", "end_date": "2023-06-30"}.
    - "from 2023/01/01 to 2023/06/30" should be {"start_date": "2023-01-01", "end_date": "2023-06-30"}.

name: filters
description:
A list of filters to apply to the query.
- Format: [{"field": "campaignName", "operator": "CONTAINS", "value": "summer"}].
- "field": The field to filter on. Must match schema.
- "operator": Must be one of these supported values: EQUALS,NOT_EQUALS,IN,NOT_IN,REGEXP_MATCH,NOT_REGEXP_MATCH,CONTAINS,NOT_CONTAINS,GREATER_THAN,GREATER_THAN_EQUALS,LESS_THAN,LESS_THAN_EQUALS.
- "value": Can be a string, number, regex, or a list of strings.
- Special Case: When a user specifies multiple string values for the CONTAINS operator, use the REGEX_MATCHES operator to combine them. Note that this should be a full regex match, not partial. For example, if the user says "campaignName that contains 'summer' or 'spring'", then use a REGEX_MATCHES operator with the pattern ".*(summer|spring).*".

name: order_by
description:
A list of objects containing "field" and "order".
- for example: [{"field": "session", "order": "DESC"},"{"field": "country", "order": "ASC"}].
- "field": The field to sort by. Must match schema.
- "order": The order to sort by, must be one of "ASC", "DESC"
- Order by is optional. Should be specified by the user if sorting is desired. For example, if the user says "top 10 campaigns sorted by sessions," then sorting by "sessions" is required.

name: limit
description:
The maximum number of rows to return.
- Defaults to 100.
- Use only if specified by the user. For example, if the user says 'top 10'.
- Do not use for aggregate results like 'total clicks'.

name: compared_to
description:
The date period to compare to. Must be one of 2 values: "previous_period" or "previous_year".
- This is optional, user must say "compared to" to use this. Don't ever assume this.
- Here are some how users might ask for this:
    - "this week compared to last week" should be "previous_period".
    - "last week compared to previous week" should be "previous_period".
    - "this month compared to last month" should be "previous_period".     
    - "compared to same month last year" should be "previous_year".

The d20 system supports complex dice roll expressions, including: - Basic rolls, like "4d6" (roll 4 six-sided dice). - Dice roll modifiers, like "1d20+4" (roll a twenty-sided die and add 4). - Multiple Dice roll expressions in one call via comma separated list. Such as "4d6kh3,4d6kh3,4d6kh3,4d6kh3,4d6kh3,4d6kh3". - Advantage and disadvantage rolls, like "1d20adv" (roll two twenty-sided dice and take the higher result). - Dice roll expressions with multiple parts, like "2d6+1d4" (roll two six-sided dice and one four-sided die and add the results). - Dropping the highest/lowest roll, like "4d6dl1" (roll four six-sided dice and drop the lowest roll) is the wrong syntax. The correct syntax for rolling 4 six-sided dice and dropping the lowest roll is "4d6kh3". This stands for "roll 4 six-sided dice, keep the highest 3".  - Sending "help" as the expression will return a list of available dice roll expression types and the URL to the plugin's help page.

name: query
description: A query to find relevant research papers. Ask research questions related to scientific topics, like 'impact of climate change on GDP' or 'benefits of mindfulness meditation'. Ask broad yes/no questions, explore relationships between concepts or the effects of a concept. Use technical language to maximize the relevance to academic text. For example, if user asks 'Why does being cold make you sick?', search 'Does cold temperature exposure increase the risk of illness?'. Omit words that we have filters for such as study types and years and instead use the filters. Omit unnecessary commands like 'latest research' and 'find papers', focus only on words likely to match the text of research papers.

name: year_min
description: The earliest publication year to consider in the search, filtering out papers published before this year. You must only use this filter when the user asks for information after a certain date. An example of when to use this filter would be if a user asks 'show me papers about the covid vaccine published after 2020' or 'papers about immigration reform published between 2000 and 2015'. Do not use this filter unless the user specifically asks for it. If you use this filter without the user specifically including a date or 'recent research', you will be penalized.

name: year_max
description: The latest publication year to consider in the search, filtering out papers published after this year. You must only use this filter when the user asks for information before a certain date. An example of when to use this filter would be if a user asks 'show me papers about the covid vaccine published before 2023' or 'papers about immigration reform published between 2000 and 2015'. Only use this filter when a specific year restriction is requested by the user

name: study_types
description: List of study types to include in the search, such as RCT, Meta-Analysis, Systematic Review, Observational Study, Case Report etc. Do NOT use this filter unless users specifically mention one of the study types. For example, if a user asks 'does zinc help with depression? show me responses from RCTs' or 'I need to find a systematic review on the effects of spanking on children', then you may use this filter. If the user does not specifically mention a type of study, and you use this filter, you will be penalized.

name: human
description: Set to true to limit the search to studies involving human subjects. You must only use this filter if the users asks for information from human studies. An example of when to use this filter would be if a user asks 'what are the effects of magnesium on sleep? only show me studies conducted on humans'. Only use this filter when it is specifically asked for by the user

name: sample_size_min
description: The minimum sample size of the studies to include in the search, targeting studies with a larger participant base. You must only use this filter when the user asks for studies with a large sample size or over a certain number of participants. An example of when to use this filter would be if a user asks 'what are the effects of magnesium on sleep? only show me studies with large sample sizes' in this case set the filter to ~100. Only use this filter when it is specifically asked for by the user

name: sjr_max
description: The maximum SJR quartile (1-4) of the journals to include. This helps set a threshold for journal prestige, where 1 is the highest quartile. You must only use this filter when the user asks for information from higher-ranked journals. An example of when to use this filter would be if a user asks 'Produce me a rrl on interest rates in the economy only from the best journals' in this case set the fiter to 1. Only use this filter when it is specficially asked for by the user

name: country_name
description:
Full name of the country where trails are located. If the user does not explicitly specify the `country_name` property, the `country_name` property should be deduced from the `state_name`, `city_name`, or `area_name` property. 

For example, if user asks for 'trails in San Francisco', automatically set the `country_name` property to 'United States' and the `state_name` property to 'California'.

If the user specifies they're interested in trails around the world, set `country_name` to 'world'.

This property MUST always be populated.

name: state_name
description:
Full name of the state or region where trails are located. If not given, the `state_name` property should be deduced from the `city_name`, or `area_name` property. 

For example, if user asks for trails in Rochester, automatically set `country_name` to 'United States' and `state_name`='New Hampshire'.

This property MUST be populated whenever a user mentions a specific state, city, or area. 

Always ensure the state or region name is in its full form, not abbreviated.

name: city_name
description:
This property represents the full name of the city or town where trails are located and MUST be populated if a user specifies a city in their query.

To determine its value:
1. If the user explicitly mentions a city or town, use that city's full name. For instance, if a user says 'trails in San Francisco', set `city_name` to 'San Francisco'.
2. Do NOT populate this property if the user's query is about specific parks, forests, or wilderness areas. For example, if the user asks for trails in Yellowstone, omit the `city_name` property entirely.

Always ensure the city or town name is in its full form, not abbreviated or shortened.

name: area_name
description:
This property represents the full name of a national, state, city, or local park, forest, or wilderness area and MUST be populated if a user specifies such an area in their query.

To determine its value:
1. If the user explicitly mentions a specific park, forest, or wilderness area, use its full name. For instance, if a user says 'trails in Tahoe', set `area_name` to 'Tahoe National Forest'.
2. If the user provides a well-known abbreviation or shortened name of an area, deduce the full name. For example, if the user asks for trails in 'Yosemite', set `area_name` to 'Yosemite National Park'.

Always ensure the area name is in its complete and accurate form.

name: location_helper
description:
This property specifies if the user wants to find trails "in" or "near" the request of their specified location.

To determine the appropriate value:
1. If the user provides a broad or non-specific location, such as a state or a country (i.e. if area_name and city_name are not populated), then 'location_helper' should ALWAYS be set to 'in', regardless of the user's phrasing.
2. If the user specifies a more granular or specific location, like a city or an area (i.e. if area_name or city_name is populated), then the value can be set to 'near' if the user's query indicates proximity (e.g. 'trails near...'). 

For clarity:
- If a user says 'trails in San Francisco' or 'trails in Yellowstone National Park', then 'location_helper' should be set to 'in'.
- If a user says 'trails near San Francisco' or 'trails near Yellowstone National Park', then 'location_helper' should be set to 'near'.
- If a user says 'trails in California' or 'trails in the United States', then 'location_helper' should be set to 'in'.
- If a user says 'trails near California' or 'trails near the United States', then 'location_helper' should be set to 'in'.

name: radius
description:
This property specifies the search radius centered around a given location, represented IN METERS. It's crucial to determine its value based on the user's query and the `location_helper` property.

To determine its value:
1. If `location_helper` is set to 'in', DO NOT populate this property.
2. If `location_helper` is set to 'near':
  - If the user provides a specific distance, convert that distance to meters and use it. For example, if a user says 'trails within 10 miles of Greenpoint, Brooklyn', set `radius` to 16093 meters.
  - If the user doesn't specify a distance, default `radius` to 32187 meters (approximately 20 miles). Ensure to notify the user of this default value in the response.

Always ensure the value for `radius` is an integer. If conversions result in a float, round up or down to the nearest whole number.

name: sort_by_dist_bool
description:
If the user explicitly emphasizes that they would like the results sorted by distance (e.g. 'closest trails to Seattle'), then `sort_by_dist_bool` should be set to `true`. 

If the user simply says that they're interested in results near a location, assume that the user wants their results returned in the default popularity-based order.

name: query
description:
The 'query' property is a text-based string used to filter trails by their names or other textual attributes.

To determine its value:
1. Extract specific trail names or textual attributes mentioned by the user. For instance, if a user asks about the 'Lands End Trail', set `query` to 'Lands End'.
2. If the user does not specify a particular trail name or attribute, this property may be left empty or omitted.

It's essential to format this property correctly, as it directly influences the accuracy of the search results.

name: num_trails
description: The 'num_trails' property specifies the number of trail recommendations the user wishes to receive.

name: raw_query
description:
The 'raw_query' property is essential and MUST be populated for every request.

It captures the user's query in its exact, unaltered form. This means capturing the user's input word for word without any modifications or omissions.

For instance, if a user says, 'Show me trails in San Francisco under 30 miles', the `raw_query` should be set to 'Show me trails in San Francisco under 30 miles'.

Accurately recording the 'raw_query' ensures that the user's original intent is preserved and can be referenced if needed.

name: filters
description:
The 'filters' property is a vital component and MUST be populated for every request, even when it seems duplicative to do so.
It is a an intricate Algiolia filter string tailored to refine search results based on user preferences.

Here's how to construct the `filters` string:
1. **Parameters**: The string is built using a combination of specific parameters. Some of them are of a string-enum type: `activities`, `features`, `difficulty_rating`, `route_type`, `visitor_usage`. Others are numeric: `length`, `elevation_gain`, `highest_point`, `avg_rating`, and `duration_minutes`. Only these parameters should be integrated into the `filters` string and these parameters should NEVER be used outside of the filter string property.
2. **Boolean Operators**: Use `AND` and `OR` operators to combine conditions. Always group conditions with parentheses for clarity. For example, for a query like 'Dog-friendly trails in San Francisco under 5 hours', the string would be: `(features:dogs OR features:dogs-leash) AND duration_minutes < 300`.
3. **Numerical Parameters**: For parameters `length`, `elevation_gain`, `highest_point`, `avg_rating`, and `duration_minutes`, use "=" for exact matches and "<" or ">" for comparisons. For instance, "duration_minutes=360" represents trails taking 6 hours, whereas "duration_minutes>240" represents trails taking more than 4 hours.
4. **String-Enum Parameters**: Use a colon ":" for these. For instance, "features:dogs" or "activities:backpacking".
5. **Default Value**: If the user doesn't specify any filtering criteria, set the `filters` parameter to an empty string.

Below are the details of the various parameters (separated by horizontal rules) that can be used as part of the `filters` string:

---

The 'activities' parameter is utilized to filter trails based on specific outdoor activities they accommodate.

Match the user's mentioned activities with the provided enums. 
For instance, if a user says 'trails with bike paths', then `(activities:mountain-biking OR activities:road-biking)` should be included in the `filters` string.

Here is a dictionary describing the ONLY activities that are supported by this API:

- backpacking: Outdoor recreation of carrying gear on one's back while hiking for more than a day.
- birding: Bird-watching. Use this when the user is interested in watching birds.
- camping: Camping. Use this when the user is asking for trails that go to, from, or through a campsite.
- xc-skiing: The sport of skiing across the countryside (cross-country skiing), often through woods and usually on relatively flat terrain.
- fishing: Fishing. Use this when the user is interested in trails that go to, from, or through a fishing spot.
- hiking: The activity of going for long walks in the country or woods. Use this whenever a user mentions hiking.
- horses: Use this when the user is looking for horseback riding trails or specifies that they are an equestrian.
- mountain-biking: Mountain biking is a sport of riding bicycles off-road, often over rough terrain, usually using specially designed mountain bikes.
- off-road-driving: Off-roading is the activity of driving or riding in a vehicle on unpaved surfaces such as sand, dirt, gravel, riverbeds, mud, snow, rocks, and other natural terrain.
- paddle-sports: Any sport involving the propulsion of a watercraft by means of a paddle. Kayaking and canoeing are paddlesports.
- road-biking: Road cycling is the a form of cycling in which cyclists ride on paved roadways.
- rock-climbing: The sport or activity of climbing rock faces, especially with the aid of ropes and special equipment.
- scenic-driving: Scenic driving. Driving routes through areas with good views.
- skiing: The action of traveling over snow on skis, especially as a sport or recreation.
- snowshoeing: A very specific activity of walking over snow wearing snowshoes.
- trail-running: Use this when the user is interested in trails supporting any running activity (running, jogging, trail running, etc.)
- walking: Use this when the user is interested in trails supporting any casual walking activity (walking, strolling, etc.)
- bike-touring: Bike touring. Bicycle touring can range from single-day trips to extended travels spanning weeks or months.
- via-ferrata: A specific type of climbing route found in the Alps and certain other Alpine locations where the user hangs or clips onto cables.
- whitewater-kayaking: The activity of paddling a kayak on whitewater (turbulent water).

If the user's mentioned activities don't align with the provided enums, inform the user of the available activity options and seek further clarification.
It's crucial to distinguish between `activities` and `features`. Activities typically involve actions, often ending in '-ing' (e.g. 'hiking', 'biking'). NEVER list features, such as 'dogs' or 'waterfall', under `activities`. Always cross-reference with the provided enums to ensure accuracy.
Only apply these activity-related parameters if the user explicitly mentions them in their query. For example, if the user simply implies that they are looking for trails "in the winter", don't automoatically assume that the user is looking for skiing or snowshoeing related trails.

---

The 'features' parameter is employed to filter trails based on specific characteristics or attributes they possess, either inherent to the trail or related to its accessibility/suitability.

Pay close attention to the user's specific requirements regarding dogs:
  - If a user inquires about 'dog-friendly trails', then use `(features:dogs AND features:dogs-leash)`. 
  - If a user specifies wanting trails where dogs are allowed without leashes, then use `features:dogs` only.
  - If a user specifies a preference for trails where dogs must be on leashes, then use `features:dogs-leash` only.
  - In the absence of specific instructions about leashes, include both ['dogs', 'dogs-leash'] to cover all dog-friendly trails.

Here is a dictionary describing the ONLY features that are supported by this API:

- ada: Trail is disabilities-friendly (e.g. wheelchairs, wheelchair friendly...etc)
- beach: Trail features a beach.
- cave: Trail features a cave.
- dogs: Trail is dog friendly, doesn't require a leash. 
- dogs-leash: Trail is dog friendly, but requires a leash.
- dogs-no: Trail is not dog friendly, no dogs are allowed.
- forest: Trail features a forest.
- lake: Trail features a lake.
- kids: Trail is kid/child friendly. 
- hot-springs: Trail features hot springs.
- paved: Trail is paved.
- partially-paved: Trail is partially paved.
- rails-trails: Trail follows railroad rails.
- river: Trail features a river.
- strollers: Trail is stroller friendly.
- views: Trail has good views along it.
- waterfall: Trail features a waterfall.
- wild-flowers: Trail features wild flowers.
- wildlife: Trail features wildlife (animals).
- off-trail: Trails that involve a lot of bush-whacking and route finding.
- no-shade: Trail is not situated well for users who want to avoid the sun.
- city-walk: Urban trail routes going through the middle of cities.
- historic-site: Trail is located in or by a historic site.
- pub-crawl: Trails that are representative of pub crawls, the act of visiting multiple pubs or bars in a single session. Primarily used in the UK.
- fee: Trail is not free OR requires a ticket to be purchased in order to access.

If the user's mentioned features don't correspond loosely with the provided enums, inform them of the available feature options and request further details. 
It is essential that the assistant doesn't incorrectly apply an activity type as a feature or vice-versa.

---

The 'difficulty_rating' parameter represents the trail's level of difficulty. It can be ONLY one of the following string values:

- easy: Easy trails that are suitable for all skill levels.
- moderate: Moderate trails that are suitable for those at intermediate skill levels.
- hard: Hard trails that are suitable for those at advanced skill levels and those looking for a challenge.

For example: If a user asks for 'easy trails', then `difficulty_rating:easy`.

---

The 'route_type' parameter specifies the configuration or layout of the trail. It can be ONLY one of the following string values:

- loop: The start and end points are the same.
- out-and-back: One travels to a destination and then retraces their steps back to the starting point.
- point-to-point: The trail starts and ends at different locations.

For example, if user asks for 'loop trails', then `route_type:loop`.

---

The 'visitor_usage' parameter represents the level of traffic on the trail. It can be ONLY one of the following string values:

- light: The trail is lightly trafficked - not a lot of people are typically on it.
- moderate: The trail is moderately trafficked.
- heavy: The trail is heavily trafficked - many people are typically on it.
- extreme: The trail is extremely trafficked - this is one of the busiest trails in the area.

For example, if user asks for 'trails with light to moderate trail traffic', then `visitor_usage:light OR visitor_usage:moderate`.

---

The 'length' parameter is a number that represents the length of a trail in meters.

For example, if user asks for 'trails that are 1 mile long', then `length=1609.34`.

Perform arithmetic to calculate the total length of the trail as a trip, if needed.

---

The 'elevation_gain' parameter is a number that represents the elevation gain of a trail in meters.

For example, if user asks for 'trails with 6000 ft elevation gain', then `elevation_gain=1828.8`.

---

The 'highest_point' parameter is a number that represents the highest point on a trail in meters.

For example, if user asks for 'trails with a highest point of 8000 ft', then `highest_point=2438.4`.

---

The 'avg_rating' parameter is a number that represents the average user rating for a trail based on a 5-star scale (ranges from 1 to 5).

For example, if a user asks for 'trails rated 4.2 stars', then `avg_rating=4.2'.

If the user specifies a rating outside the 1-5 range or provides a non-integer value, inform them of the available options and seek clarification.

---

The 'duration_minutes' parameter is numerical and indicates the average time, in minutes, that AllTrails users typically take to complete a trail.

For example, if they ask for 'trails that can be completed in an hour', then `duration_minutes=60`

---

description: O campo "tarefa" define os requisitos e objetivos específicos para a geração do conteúdo. Isso inclui instruções detalhadas sobre o que precisa ser realizado por meio da escrita, como o tópico principal a ser abordado, quaisquer argumentos ou perspectivas específicas a serem apresentadas e o resultado desejado ou impacto da peça. Este campo serve como uma diretriz para o processo de criação de conteúdo, garantindo que a escrita não apenas adere às diretrizes fornecidas, mas também efetivamente alcança seu propósito pretendido, seja ele informar, persuadir, entreter ou educar o público.

name: summary
description: O campo "resumo" encapsula uma visão geral concisa do conteúdo da escrita, apresentando os temas centrais, pontos-chave e objetivos primários da peça. Este resumo breve, mas abrangente, serve como um roteiro, guiando a direção geral e o foco da escrita, garantindo que permaneça alinhada com a mensagem e propósito pretendidos ao longo do processo de desenvolvimento. Este resumo não só ajuda a manter a coerência e relevância, mas também fornece uma prévia clara do que o leitor pode esperar do conteúdo completo.

name: reference
description: O campo "referência" é uma coleção selecionada de informações obtidas da Internet através do WebPilot, ou fornecidas pelo usuário, especificamente adaptadas para enriquecer e apoiar a tarefa de escrita em questão. Envolve um processo seletivo onde dados relevantes, fatos e insights relacionados ao tópico são coletados, garantindo que o conteúdo não seja apenas bem informado e preciso, mas também esteja alinhado com os requisitos específicos e objetivos do projeto de escrita. Este campo atua como uma base, fornecendo uma rica fonte de informações verificadas e pertinentes a partir das quais o artigo ou conteúdo é elaborado. Este campo seria longo.

name: style
description: O campo "estilo" na criação de conteúdo é um framework detalhado que abrange três componentes pivôs - o tom ou estilo de escrita, o público-alvo e o meio de publicação. Este campo é estruturado como "[estilo de escrita específico], visando [público-alvo], usando [estilo de linguagem], inspirado por [criador de conteúdo notável]". O elemento de estilo de escrita varia de formal e analítico a informal e envolvente, definindo o tom geral. O aspecto do público-alvo identifica o grupo de leitores específico, como estudantes, profissionais ou o público em geral, adaptando a complexidade e relevância do conteúdo. O estilo de linguagem, seja acadêmico, coloquial ou técnico, molda a abordagem linguística. O componente final, inspirado por um criador de conteúdo notável, serve como uma referência para o tom e a abordagem desejados, como "analítico e conciso, voltado para profissionais de negócios, usando linguagem profissional, inspirado por um renomado jornalista de negócios". Essa definição clara e estruturada garante que o conteúdo esteja efetivamente alinhado com as necessidades do público e o formato de publicação.

The python pandas code to run in the notebook (the next cell to execute). This is being executed in a remote Jupyter notebook.
You should always start sessions by: - reading in any files that will be used - Getting the head or inspecting the data in some way - Troubleshooting errors
- If there's issues with the data, work with the user to remove rows that are causing issues, clean the data, or otherwise get it into a shape that doesn't result in constant errors.
- When reading CSVs, if you don't know the character encoding, try to read with UTF first and fall back to ISO-8859-1 if that fails (just use try/except, same with other sorts of things; if there's ambiguous values try a few methods and see which one works and use that moving forward).
- Troubleshoot any issues by inspecting columns and data types with .info() and .head().
- Use coerce = true with numeric data to help it avoid erroring. - !IMPORTANT! Do not use F strings. Avoid using any sorts of quotes in your outputs - use <> instead of quotes to display messages. - If something has failed multiple times, switch strategies. - Deal with nan values before plotting data. - Before creating line plots, make sure that the data is sorted by the values on the x-axis.

name: style
description: The "style" field in content creation is a detailed framework encompassing three pivotal components - the writing tone or style, the target audience, and the publication medium. This field is structured as "[specific writing style], aimed at [target audience], using [language style], inspired by [notable content creator]." The writing style element ranges from formal and analytical to casual and engaging, setting the overall tone. The target audience aspect identifies the specific reader group, such as students, professionals, or the general public, tailoring the content's complexity and relevance. The language style, whether academic, colloquial, or technical, shape the linguistic approach. The final component, inspired by a notable content creator, serves as a reference for the desired tone and approach, like "analytical and concise, aimed at business professionals, using professional language, inspired by a renowned business journalist." This clear and structured definition ensures the content is effectively aligned with the audience's needs and the publication's format.

description: For example, if the user asks for "cost on LinkedIn ads last month", then call getLinkedInAdsMetricsList and getLinkedInAdsBreakdownsList to retrieve the latest up-to-date info about how to compose a linkedin_ads_request. A metric is a quantitative measurement. It represents data that can be measured and expressed in numbers. Metrics are used to track performance or behavior. Examples include clicks, impressions, conversions, revenue, etc. A breakdown is a qualitative attribute or descriptor. It provides context for metrics by categorizing or segmenting them. Breakdowns are text. Examples include country, channel, campaign name, etc. DO NOT include Date, Month, Quarter or Year in the list of breakdowns in any of the requests below. name: range
description: The range the values cover, in [A1 notation](/sheets/api/guides/concepts#cell). For output, this range indicates the entire requested range, even though the values will exclude trailing rows and columns. When appending values, this field represents the range to search for a table, after which values will be appended.

name: majorDimension
description: The major dimension of the values. For output, if the spreadsheet data is: `A1=1,B1=2,A2=3,B2=4`, then requesting `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=ROWS` will return `[[1,2],[3,4]]`, whereas requesting `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=COLUMNS` will return `[[1,3],[2,4]]`. For input, with `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=ROWS` then `[[1,2],[3,4]]` will set `A1=1,B1=2,A2=3,B2=4`. With `range=A1:B2,majorDimension=COLUMNS` then `[[1,2],[3,4]]` will set `A1=1,B1=3,A2=2,B2=4`. When writing, if this field is not set, it defaults to ROWS.

name: values
description: The data that was read or to be written. This is an array of arrays, the outer array representing all the data and each inner array representing a major dimension. Each item in the inner array corresponds with one cell. For output, empty trailing rows and columns will not be included. For input, supported value types are: bool, string, and double. Null values will be skipped. To set a cell to an empty value, set the string value to an empty string.
